docs.title: Parkinson's disease biomarker model
docs.text: A LinkML data model for Parkinson's disease cohort data: participants, visits, diagnoses, phenotypes, clinical rating scales, specimens, and fluid and imaging biomarkers. Value sets are bound to ontologies, cross-field rules are enforced at validation time, and every measurement carries provenance. All example data is synthetic.

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
The model has two layers.

  • Core (core.yaml): a disease-agnostic model of a cohort study. A StudyDataset holds flat lists of records that refer to each other by identifier, so each class maps to one table. The dataset, diagnosis and clinical assessment classes are abstract: a disease module subclasses them to bind its own value sets.
  • Parkinson's module (pd_biomarker_model.yaml): imports the core and narrows it. ParkinsonsDiagnosis restricts the condition to parkinsonian disorders and adds diagnostic criteria; ParkinsonsClinicalAssessment binds the instrument to MDS-UPDRS, MoCA and Hoehn and Yahr and adds score-range and medication-state rules. Another disease area would add its own module in the same way, without changing the core.

See the model diagram and the schema reference.

docs.title: Value sets
docs.text:
• Diseases: MONDO, dynamic (descendants of parkinsonian disorder, multiple system atrophy, progressive supranuclear palsy and Lewy body dementia)
  • Phenotypes: HPO, dynamic (descendants of Phenotypic abnormality)
  • Specimen types: UBERON
  • Brain regions for imaging: UBERON, dynamic (parts of brain)
  • Assay technologies: OBI and NCIT
  • Platforms and panel versions: PRIDE
  • Units: UCUM codes, mapped to UO
  • Rating scales: LOINC and NCIT
  • Sex, laterality and measurement type: PATO and STATO

Each permissible value records its ontology term in meaning and the term's label in title. Where no exact term exists, the value carries a broad_mappings, close_mappings or related_mappings entry instead of a meaning.

docs.title: Standalone vocabularies
docs.text: The fixed value sets are also exported as standalone vocabularies in vocabularies/, ready to load into a terminology system: one SKOS concept scheme and one OWL ontology per value set, plus a TSV of all values. Each value has its own IRI under https://w3id.org/pd-biomarker-model/vocab/ and links to its ontology terms with SKOS mapping properties. Dynamic value sets are exported as their defining query (source ontology, root terms, relationships) rather than as a member list, because their members follow each ontology release.

docs.title: Validation
docs.text:
linkml-validate --config validation.yaml runs three layers of checks:

  • Structure and rules (JSON Schema generated from the schema, closed to undeclared slots): required slots, ranges, patterns, minimum and maximum values, and cross-field rules. Units must match the measurement type (a ratio is dimensionless, a concentration is in pg/mL or ng/mL, a SomaScan or Olink value is in RFU or NPX); categorical results carry no value or unit; imaging values need a brain region and laterality and no specimen; a person curator is identified by an ORCID; each rating scale has its score range; MDS-UPDRS Part III and Hoehn and Yahr need the medication state.
  • Ontology terms: values of dynamic value sets must be in the expanded ontology branch, checked against a committed cache so validation runs offline. A separate check confirms every meaning term exists, is not obsolete and has the label recorded in title.
  • Cross-record rules: every reference resolves to a record in the dataset, identifiers are unique, no visit precedes enrolment, a measurement's specimen was collected at the same visit, and symptom onset does not follow diagnosis.

The examples include one invalid file per rule.

docs.title: Identifiers and versioning
docs.text:
• Schema URI: https://w3id.org/pd-biomarker-model; record identifiers are CURIEs in the pdbm: namespace.
  • Analytes are identified by UniProtKB accession, so values from different proteomics platforms can be linked to the same protein, with the platform's own reagent identifier (SomaScan SeqId or Olink assay ID) kept on the measurement.
  • The schema follows semantic versioning; see the changelog.

docs.title: About
docs.text:
The Parkinson's disease biomarker model is maintained by Salvatore Barbagallo and released under the MIT licence.

All example records are synthetic. They are generated from public standards and invented values, and contain no data or variable definitions from any real study.

docs.title: Changelog
docs.text:
All notable changes to the schema are recorded here. The format follows Keep a Changelog, and the schema uses Semantic Versioning:

  • major: a change that can make previously valid data invalid (removed or renamed classes, slots or permissible values; narrower ranges; new required slots or rules)
  • minor: a backwards-compatible addition (new optional slots, classes or permissible values)
  • patch: documentation, descriptions or mappings only

Before 1.0.0, a change that would need a major version increases the minor version instead.

docs.title: Changed
docs.text: • StudyDataset and Diagnosis in the core are abstract, like ClinicalAssessment. Data uses the disease module's classes (ParkinsonsStudyDataset, ParkinsonsDiagnosis), and the generated SQL has no tables for the core classes.

docs.title: Added
docs.text:
• Disease-agnostic core schema (core.yaml): StudyDataset, Participant, Visit, Diagnosis, PhenotypeObservation, ClinicalAssessment, Specimen, Analyte, Assay, BiomarkerMeasurement and ProvenanceMixin.
  • Parkinson's module (pd_biomarker_model.yaml): ParkinsonsStudyDataset, ParkinsonsDiagnosis and ParkinsonsClinicalAssessment.
  • Value sets bound to MONDO, HPO, UBERON, OBI, PATO, NCIT, STATO, UO, PRIDE and LOINC; dynamic value sets for diseases, phenotypes, brain regions and parkinsonian disorders.
  • Cross-field rules for units by measurement type, quantitative versus categorical results, imaging versus specimen measurements, curator identifiers, instrument score ranges and medication state.

docs.title: Curation guidelines
docs.text: These rules govern how a source variable is mapped to an ontology term. The gold-standard mapping follows them, the mapping agent is instructed with them, and a reviewer applies them when accepting, rejecting or correcting a proposal.

docs.title: What is mapped
docs.text:
Each source variable is mapped once, to the concept the variable records. A yes/no variable for "rest tremor" records the phenotype Resting tremor; a variable holding a serum NfL concentration records the laboratory test for NfL mass concentration in serum or plasma.

Read the name, the description and the unit together. Abbreviations are resolved from the description and unit, never from the name alone (SAA is a seed amplification assay here, not serum amyloid A; PD is Parkinson's disease, not peritoneal dialysis; RBD is REM sleep behaviour disorder, not a receptor-binding domain).

docs.title: Target vocabularies
docs.text:
Use the first vocabulary that applies:

  1. Diagnoses (a disease present or absent): MONDO.
  2. Signs and symptoms: HPO, even when a disease of the same name exists in MONDO.
  3. Laboratory tests: LOINC. The code must agree with the variable on component, specimen, property and, if the variable states it, method. The unit decides the property: a mass unit (pg/mL, ng/L, mg/L) takes a Mass/volume code, a molar unit (pmol/L, µmol/L) a Moles/volume code.
  4. Rating scales: LOINC when a code exists for the same instrument version and score; otherwise NCIT. MDS-UPDRS is not the original UPDRS, and the Hoehn and Yahr stage rated in MDS-UPDRS is not the modified Hoehn and Yahr scale.
  5. Analyte measurements without a LOINC code, including SomaScan (RFU) and Olink (NPX) values: the protein in NCIT, with skos:relatedMatch. A relative unit is never mapped to a concentration test.
  6. Study administration and demographics: NCIT (CDISC concepts).

Only current terms are used; obsolete terms are replaced by their successor.

docs.title: Predicates
docs.text:
• skos:exactMatch: the term means the same as the variable, including specimen, property and instrument version.
  • skos:broadMatch: the term is more general than the variable (a questionnaire for one of its total scores; Cognitive impairment for PD mild cognitive impairment).
  • skos:narrowMatch: the term is more specific than the variable.
  • skos:relatedMatch: associated but neither equivalent nor hierarchical (a measurement and its analyte; a carrier status and the genetic disease).

When no term meets these rules, the object is sssom:NoTermFound. Proposing no term is better than proposing a wrong one.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: Every mapping records who made it (author_id: an ORCID for a person, a versioned agent identifier for an AI agent), how (mapping_justification: semapv:ManualMappingCuration for a person, semapv:LexicalMatching or semapv:SemanticSimilarityThresholdMatching for the agent), when (mapping_date) and, for agent proposals, with what (mapping_tool, confidence). The curator_type column records whether the author was a person or an AI agent. A reviewer's decision adds reviewer_id and a comment; corrected proposals keep the agent's original term in the comment.
